Author: Sudhir Agarwal
Bench: Sudhir Agarwal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
Court No. - 34
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 1578 of 2006

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Applicant :- ITC Ltd. And Another Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Raghav Nayar Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate,C.K.Pareekh, Deepak Singh  Hon'ble Sudhir Agarwal,J.
1.

Heard Sri Navin Sinha, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Sri Raghav Nayar, Advocate for applicants, learned A.G.A. for State and Sri Deepak Singh, Advocate for Respondent-2.
2.

Applicants have invoked jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "Cr.P.C.") with a prayer to quash the proceedings of Criminal Complaint Case No. 3057 of 1999, under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 1954") and order dated 02.08.2005 dismissing Criminal Revision No. 321 of 2004.
3.
It is contended that a sample of Chane Ki Dal of the canteen maintained in the premises of Applicant-1 was taken by Food Inspector on 31.12.1997.
As per complaint filed by said Food Inspector the sample sent for examination by Public Analyst who submitted its report dated Itc Ltd.

And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 3 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187449698/
1 13.02.1998 stating that it did not conform with the standard prescribed under Act, 1954 and,
therefore, comes within the ambit of "adulterated food item".

Consequently a letter dated 11.04.1998 was sent to Applicant-1 and thereafter a complaint under Section 7(1) read with Section 2(ia)(h) of Act, 1954 of Act was filed by State of U.P. through Sri P.P. Tiwari, Food Inspector, Nagar Palika Parishad, Saharanpur in the Court of First Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate/ Special Judicial Magistrate (Economic Offences), Saharanpur vide complaint dated 12.08.1999.

entities.text: First Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate/ Special Judicial Magistrate (Economic Offences), Saharanpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Chief Medical Officer, Saharanpur gave consent under Section 20 of Act, 1954 on 28.07.1997.
4.

On the aforesaid complaint, Magistrate has passed summoning order dated 12.08.1999 which is challenged in this application alongwith all proceedings on the ground that there was a complete disregard of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 inasmuch as no notice alongwith Public Analyst Report was served upon applicants and, therefore, entire proceedings are vitiated in law.

My attention was drawn to paras 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 of complaint, which reads as under:
"6.

That on receipt of the part of the sample the P.A. to the Govt. of U.P. Lucknow delivered his report No. 7/7 dated 13.2.98 to the local health authority and declared the sample of Chane Ke Dal adulterated, the report of P.A. is below:-

7.

That after receiving the report of Public Analyst I enquired through a Registered letter dated 11.4.98 from the person named at S. No. 1 to know the name and designation of the person who was to be incharge of, and responsible to the Company for the conduct of the business of canteen nominated by the Company under sub-section 2 of the Section 17 of the P.F.A. Act at the time of taking sample of Chane Ki Dal (Photostat copy of the letter is attached).

8. That in reply of my letter dated 11.4.98 a letter No. IIRD/98/ 269 dated 24.4.98 signed by Human Resources Manager on behalf of the I.T.C. Ltd. Saharanpur was Itc Ltd. And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 3 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187449698/
2 received for giving time till May 30, 1998 and later on a letter dated 30th May, 1998 signed by Human Resources Manager I.T.C. Ltd., Saharanpur was received which does not disclose the name of nominee as required by me.

9. That the persons named at S. No. 1 and S. No. 2 have committed an offence U/s 7(1) read with Section 2(ia)(h) of the P.F.A. Act and read with Rule 44-A of the P.F.A.
Rules punishable U/s 16(1-A) of the P.F.A. Act.
10. That Chief Medical Officer (Local Health Authority) Saharanpur has given his written consent on 28.7.97 for the institution of the prosecution in the Court U/s 20 of the P.F.A. Act."

5. Letter dated 11.04.198 is also on record as Annexure-2 to application and it reads as under:
"I want to bring to your kind notice that the sample of "CHANE KE DAL" Food article bearing Code & S. No. of L.H.R. PP/97/ 257/ 257 dated 31.12.97 was taken by me in exercise of the powers under the provisions of Section 10 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 from the canteen managed by your Company situated within the premises of I.T.C. Ltd., Saharanpur and the same was analyzed and found adulterated by the Public Analyst to the Government of U.P. Lucknow.

In this connection, I would like to know the name and designation of the person if any, who was to be In charge of, and responsible to, the Company for the conduct of the business of the Company nominated by the Co. under sub section 2 of the Section 17 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 at the time of taking sample so that necessary legal action be taken.
An early reply of this letter is requested."
6. It is said that aforesaid letter is not at all a compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 inasmuch as copy of Public Analyst Report was not given to applicants.
Only certain inquiry was made from Applicant-1.
It is further contended that requirement of Section 13(2) is mandatory and non compliance thereof is vitiated the entire proceedings.

7. Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 reads as under:
"13. Report of public analyst......
(2) On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under section 14A, forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired,
Itc Ltd. And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 3 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187449698/
3 either or both of them may make an application to the court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory."
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, Rule 9B of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as "Rules, 1955") reads as under:
"9-B. Local (Health) Authority to send report to person concerned:- The Local (Health) Authority shall within a period of ten days after the institution of prosecution forward a copy of the report of the result of analysis in Form III delivered to him under sub-rule (3) of Rule 7, by registered post or by hand, as may be appropriate, to the person from whom the sample of the article was taken by the Food Inspector, and simultaneously also to the person if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under Section 14-A of the Act:
Provided that where the sample conforms to the provisions of the Act or the rules made thereunder, and no prosecution is intended under sub-section (2) or no action is intended under sub-Section 2(E) of Section 13 of the Act, the Local (Health)
Authority shall intimate the result to the Vendor from whom the sample has been taken and also to the person whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under Section 14A of the Act, within 10 days from the receipt of the report from the Public Analyst."
9.

Thus after institution of prosecution, authority concerned is obliged to sent a notice alongwith copy of Public Analyst Report to accused persons within 10 days but in the present case same has not been complied with.

In the counter affidavit respondent-authorities have relied on a letter dated 11.04.1998 contents whereof I have already quoted and it is evident that aforesaid letter cannot be construed by any stretch of imagination to be a compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954.

10. Effect of non compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 has been considered by Supreme Court very recently in Vijendra Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 1167 of 2019) (Arising out of S.L.P. (Criminal) No. 4314 of 2015) decided on 31.07.2019 and in para 15 of judgment, Court has said as under:
"The very purpose of furnishing such report is to enable the Accused to seek for reference to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis if the Accused is dissatisfied with the report.

entities.text: Vijendra Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 1167 of 2019)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such safeguard provided to the Accused Under Section 13(2) of the Act is a valuable right.

In that view even if the despatch of the report on 07.04.1980 is taken as substantial compliance though it is beyond the period of 10 days from 18.03.1980 i.e., the date on which the prosecution was lodged, in the absence of there being proof of delivery of the report to the Accused; in the instant facts the valuable right available to the Accused/Appellant to seek for reference within the period of 10 days stands defeated.

In that circumstance when the Appellant/Accused is made to Itc Ltd. And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 3 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187449698/
4 suffer the penal consequences, it will have to be construed strictly.

entities.text: Itc Ltd. And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 3 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the facts and circumstances of this case, since as already noticed above the report of the Analyst has not in fact been served on the Appellant and the mere despatch of the report as per the statement of PW-2 was not sufficient."
(emphasis added)

11. Therefore, as a proposition of law, it cannot be doubted that prosecution, when challenged, must satisfy that notice issued under Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 has been served upon accused because it is right of accused and prosecution must prove that not only report of Public Analyst was sent by registered post, but it was actually served upon accused-Revisionist, which has not been done in the case in hand.
12.

Learned A.G.A. appearing for State could not dispute the aforesaid legal position and Sri Deepak Singh, Advocate appearing for Respondent-2 has simply adopted the stand taken by learned A.G.A.
and did not advance any further argument.
13. In view thereof, the application is allowed.
Proceedings in Criminal Complaint Case No. 3057 of 1999, under Section 7/16 of Act, 1954 and order dated 02.08.2005 are hereby quashed.
